US: Oldendorf's close bombardment force materially improves suppression and damages visible coastal/AA positions, but deep defenses remain. TF58 has 16 fast carrier decks in the battle system, with roughly 905-990 carrier aircraft ready after the 11-13 Jun attrition/repairs; carrier groups rotate through refueling rather than all launching over Saipan at once.

Japan_mobile: Five-carrier core 358-380 ready plus six secondary carriers 145-180 combat-usable. Taiho is first-cycle integrated; A7M remains combat zero. Yamato/Musashi/Nagato and all four surviving Kongo-class fast battleships remain in the A-GO battle system.
Japan_surface_delta: Historical KON debit is absent; Hiei/Kirishima survive; Inazuma/Minazuki/Tanikaze/Harusame are additional surviving destroyer assets relative to the historical mid-June screen, and Shiratsuyu survives 14 Jun centerline.
ISR: A US submarine now has a credible major-fleet eastbound contact, though not a complete Japanese OOB. Japanese fleet ISR still lacks a fresh TF58 task-group fix.
next_focus: 15 Jun D-Day: Saipan landing, local Japanese air/shore/tank reaction, US carrier disposition after submarine warning, and Japanese main-force movement through the Philippine Sea.
